🎙
Press conference
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin following visit to China
(Shenzhen, November 19, 2026)
Key points
:
• [During the
trilateral meeting
with the Chinese and US leaders] we talked about security matters in the broad sense of the word, about
preventing the proliferation of weapons
of mass destruction, nuclear weapons. We talked about issues
pertaining to freedom of navigation.
<...> Our discussion was held in a completely open and very candid atmosphere. It helped us
understand each other better
, and I think that
this created conditions for future arrangements
.
• We discussed some issues related to the activities of certain organisations, such as the International Criminal Court (
#ICC
), which is
clearly overstepping its mandate and making political rather than legal decisions.
• I have no doubt that
President Trump is genuinely committed to resolving conflicts
, including the conflict in Ukraine, and he is sincerely interested in
improving bilateral relations
across a range of areas, including, of course, the US-Russia relationship, which matters to us. <...> We must deal with realities as they are, and we hope that
this positive disposition will endure.
•
It wasn’t us who started the war.
We did not start any war at all. However,
hostilities had been ongoing
there for eight years: a war, in effect.
We are simply trying to bring it to an end
by providing assistance to the states that we did not recognise at first, but have now recognised, and with which we have
concluded mutual assistance treaties.
I
reminded
our colleagues of this today.
• Compromises have been reached and supported by us, including
in Anchorage.
The question is
whether the other parties to the conflict
– Ukraine and, in this case, its European sponsors –
are prepared to accept them.
In other words, do they want to reach an agreement to end hostilities, to end the war, by peaceful means or not?
Judging by what we see at the moment, they DON'T.
• As I have already said,
we are ready to make compromises
. It is essential for the other participants in the [Ukraine settlement process] to recognise
the realities on the ground
and to be prepared to make compromises on their part as well. That is all. I see nothing particularly complicated about it.
All that is needed is political will.
• [For the Kyiv regime,]
there are no incentives to agree to a cessation of hostilities
and to creating conditions for a long-term – as
I have already said
,
lasting
– peace that looks to the future.
This is precisely what we are striving for.
•
The Crimean Bridge is a purely civilian facility.
<...> We will not negotiate;
we will respond to attacks on it.
And I want everyone to be aware of that. I believe our response
will be far more painful
than what the Kyiv regime has done to the bridge.
• Working within
#APEC
is of great importance to us. We set ourselves the goal of increasing our trade turnover with this region to 40% –
it now exceeds 60%
. <...> We reaffirmed
the fundamental principles of economic relations
: freedom of economic relations and the inadmissibility of various kinds of restrictions.
• The Americans keep urging us to improve relations with Europe, but
we were not the ones who damaged those relations
.
• We recognise that Ukraine has a right to security, just as Russia does. However,
no one wants to discuss Russia’s security.
And this is a crucial point for us.
• President of China Xi Jinping and President of the US Donald Trump spoke of
China’s and the United States’ interest
, as well as that of the world as a whole, in ending the conflict in Ukraine.
Russia is also interested in ending the conflict in Ukraine.
But today, the issue is not only, or even primarily, about us –
it is about the Ukrainian side.
• Russia–China relations are one of the
cornerstones
of today’s international security system. They are an important
deterrent and a key factor in maintaining global balance.

item.title: ✉️ Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s greetings to His Holiness Patriarch Kirill of Moscow and All Russia on his 80th birthday
item.description: ✉️ Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov’s greetings to His Holiness Patriarch Kirill of Moscow and All Russia on his 80th birthday (November 20, 2026) ✍️ Your Holiness, I offer you my most heartfelt greetings on the occasion of your birthday. Your long-standing primatial ministry has earned the deepest recognition both within our country and far beyond its borders. Your tireless pastoral labours and Christian selflessness help people find spiritual support in life and contribute to strengthening the moral foundations of Russian society. Your immense personal contribution to instilling patriotic values in the younger generation commands particular respect. Your support for those taking part in the special military operation, and for their families, is truly invaluable. 🤝 I greatly value our close and fruitful cooperation. I look forward to continuing this partnership for the sake of strengthening the standing of Russia and the Orthodox world , and for advancing international relations grounded in the enduring principles of equality, truth, goodness, and justice. Wishing you the best of health, many more years, and new achievements for the benefit of the Church and the Fatherland. SERGEY LAVROV

item.title: 🌟 #Victory81 On November 19, 1942, the Red Army launched its counter-offensive in the
item.description: #Victory81 🌟 On November 19, 1942, the Red Army launched its counter-offensive in the #BattleOfStalingrad — the largest, one of the most brutal and bloodiest battles of the #GreatPatrioticWar and the entire #WW2 , which turned the tide of the war. Following several months of brutal fighting against Nazi troops, superior in strength, for control of #Stalingrad , the Soviet forces seized the strategic initiative and launched the offensive along the entire front. As a result of the operation codenamed 'Uranus', the Nazi troops near Stalingrad were encircled , subsequently split into separate groups and ultimately destroyed. *** By mid-November 1942, favourable conditions had been created for the Red Army to launch a counter-offensive. Between 19 November 1942 and 2 February 1943 , Soviet units carried out Operation 'Ring', in the course of which they succeeded in encircling Nazi Paulus's 6th Army in the pocket between the Don and Volga rivers. On 31 January, Nazi Field Marshal Friedrich Paulus surrendered together with the generals and officers of his headquarters. On 2 February, the last pockets of Nazi resistance were eliminated, with military formations of Hitler's accomplices being completely destroyed . ❗️ Despite superiority in manpower and military equipment, the Nazis failed to capture Stalingrad. The Battle of Stalingrad ended in a decisive victory of the Red Army. The triumph at Stalingrad heralded the beginning of the landmark turning point in the Great Patriotic War

The Russia-China-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace adopted following the trilateral meeting
The following is the full text of the declaration:
Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation, Xi Jinping, President of the People's Republic of China, and Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America, met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The Russian and U.S. heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit. The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.
1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, Russia, China and the United States committed to reform the U.N. so that the U.N. can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security.
2. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.
3. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.
4. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

item.title: 🎙 Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky’s response to a question from Izvestia
item.description: 🎙 Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky’s response to a question from Izvestia on the possible resumption of Russian gas supplies to Germany (November 19, 2026) ❓ Question: The trial over the Nord Stream pipeline bombings began in Germany on October 14. On October 21, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said it was technically possible to supply gas to Germany through the remaining intact pipeline. Is Germany sharing information with Russia on the progress of the investigation? Under what conditions would Russia be ready to resume gas flows through that pipeline? 💬 Dmitry Lyubinsky: In the four years since the terrorist attack on the Nord Stream 1 and Nord Stream 2 pipelines, the German authorities have consistently avoided cooperating with Russia , in breach of their international obligations under agreements on mutual legal assistance in criminal matters and counter-terrorism conventions. Russia and several other countries called for an independent, open and objective international investigation under UN auspices. That proposal was rejected. It is therefore very difficult to regard either the German judicial authorities or the findings of the investigation as impartial. ☝️ Resuming gas supplies requires , first and foremost, political will and a readiness to act on the part of the German authorities. 👉 There is no sign of either.

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's
statement
on UNESCO’s consideration of the safety of journalists
(November 19, 2026)
💬
The 35th session
of the Intergovernmental Council of the International Programme for the Development of Communication
(
#IPDC
) opens on 19 November. The Council is expected to consider
the biennial report
by UNESCO Director-General
Khaled El-Enany
on the safety of journalists in 2024-2025.
❗️
Since its publication, the report has drawn
strong criticism from the journalistic community
. It
omits information
on Russian correspondents killed in terrorist attacks by the Kiev regime –
Semyon Yeryomin
,
Yulia Kuznetsova
,
Alexander Martemyanov
and
Nikita Goldin
.
The names of
many other Russian media workers
omitted from the 2022–2023 report are
still missing
, even though Russia formally notified the UNESCO Secretariat of these crimes through diplomatic channels.
👉
These omissions stem from the persistent refusal of Audrey Azoulay of France
, who served as UNESCO Director-General until November 2025,
to condemn these crimes and record the deaths of Russian media workers in UNESCO’s statistics.
Regrettably, the current Director-General’s report has thus inherited these distortions, making it
an unreliable source of data on the safety of journalists
.
Two years ago,
the controversial report
drew
objections from countries of the Global South and East
. For the first time, the Council
failed to approve it by consensus
and merely took note of it following a vote.
Russia is currently outside the IPDC Intergovernmental Council. At the upcoming session, we nevertheless intend to raise with the Director-General
the need to take due account, without distinction, of official information provided by member states on the killings of journalists
.
We will insist that UNESCO correct the errors made by its previous leadership and include in its statistics every Russian media worker who was killed. We will call on UNESCO to condemn the crimes committed against them, as provided for in the decisions of
the 1997 General Conference
and
the 2023 Executive Board
, among others.
☝️
We will press for
a review of the so-called methodology for recording the killings of media workers
, which member states have yet to approve, and for international officials to be held properly accountable.
Given
the widespread public and media attention
the report has received, we will draw the attention of the Secretariat and IPDC member states to the numerous appeals that news outlets and professional associations have sent to the Director-General
demanding justice for their fallen colleagues
.
We are convinced that this situation is
procedurally and legally unacceptable
and
raises serious moral questions
for an organisation with universal membership within the UN system whose remit includes culture, humanitarian affairs and the development of ethical standards in these areas.
We will continue to press our legitimate demands after the session
. We owe this to our profession and to
the journalists whose lives were cut short
.
🕯
We have a sacred duty to honour their memory and keep it alive.

🎙
Remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at the Plenary Session of the
#APEC
Economic Leaders’ Meeting
(Shenzhen, November 19, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
First of all, I would like
to commend China in the strongest terms
for its work as
APEC Chair
this year. We fully endorse the theme of China’s chairmanship –
Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together
.
This is an ambitious undertaking, and
APEC
, as the largest economic forum in our region,
is uniquely placed to see it through
. As our colleague from Singapore has just noted, the global economy is becoming increasingly fragmented. With challenges and threats to its stability multiplying,
APEC must bring economies together and set a constructive agenda for cooperation
.
📄
That is precisely the aim of
the draft Shenzhen Declaration
before us for approval.
Russia supports it.
It is gratifying that
the Asia-Pacific region has become one of the engines of global growth
. The region continues to grow and steadily expand its industrial, technological and logistics capabilities. Taken together, the APEC economies are forecast
to grow by 4.8%
in 2026, well above the global rate.
☝️
Let me emphasise that building constructive partnerships with Asia-Pacific economies is a strategic priority for Russia.
We are an integral part of the region and make a substantial contribution to its prosperity.
In the first eight months of this year alone,
our trade with the region’s economies grew by almost a third
, with a focus on non-energy and innovative products. Over the past ten years,
Russia’s total trade with ASEAN countries has grown by nearly 60%.
I would also like to mention the growing network of
preferential trade agreements between countries in the region and
the Eurasian Economic Union
.
Russia is actively advancing its
flagship initiative to establish a
Greater Eurasian Partnership
to create a seamless economic area across the continent. We see this partnership as
the core of regional integration
, bringing together the mechanisms of
the Eurasian Economic Union
,
the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
and
ASEAN
.
Russia supplies the Asia-Pacific region with
energy resources as well as large quantities of grain and mineral fertilisers
. In doing so, we make a significant contribution to energy and food security throughout the region. Our trading partners can always count on us for
reliable, consistent supplies of high-quality products
.
🇷🇺
Russia seeks to remain open to the world while strengthening its economy.
To that end, we continue to pursue far-reaching reforms at home, upgrade our industrial base, expand our technological capabilities and keep inflation in check.
We have fundamentally changed the structure of the Russian economy.
We are giving priority to
advanced sectors
such as digital technology, artificial intelligence and nuclear energy. As a result, Russia’s GDP has grown by
more than 10%
in real terms over the past three years, and our country ranks firmly among the world’s leading economies in terms of purchasing power parity.
Russia is keen to work as closely as possible with fellow APEC economies in
knowledge-intensive industries
. One example is
the peaceful use of nuclear energy
, a field in which
Russia is a world leader
and works closely with many partners across the region.
🤝
Russia will continue to play an active part in APEC’s work.
